verdict.rationale: PagerDuty clearly documents alert ingestion: Events API v2 takes machine events from monitoring tools, there are 750+ integrations, and events are routed to a service, whose escalation policy notifies the assigned responders. The evidence does not document routing alerts to different teams by user-defined conditions. Event Orchestration is described only as deduplicating or suppressing alerts, and orchestration rules are mentioned only as AI-recommended. missing for 10: documented user-defined conditional routing rules (e.g., routing by payload field to a specific team or service), independent hands-on corroboration of condition-based routing.

support.subject: As an SRE, alerts from my monitoring tools are ingested through documented sources and routed to the right team by conditions I define

citations.quote: The Events API v2 is a highly reliable, highly available **asynchronous API** that ingests machine events from monitoring tools and other systems
Events sent to this API are ultimately routed to a [PagerDuty service](https://support.pagerduty.com/docs/services-and-integrations) and processed.
Incidents trigger on services, and a service's escalation policy prompts notifications to on-call responders to remediate the issue.
Event Orchestration: Automatically deduplicate or suppress alerts.
automatically analyze historical events and incidents and surface recommended rules that reduce noise, improve MTTR, and accelerate automation setup
With 750+ platform integrations, PagerDuty is a leader in connecting tools, data, and AI to your incident management process.
